DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) with possible post-infectious etiology.

The patient is a 31-year-old female with a four-month history of chronic diarrhea, lower abdominal cramping relieved by defecation, urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation. She also recalls a camping trip with a sick party member. Given the relief of pain after bowel movements and the presence of mucus, this clinical picture strongly supports a diagnosis of IBS, potentially triggered by a prior Campylobacter or Salmonella infection. Do you have any known food triggers that worsen these symptoms, and have you noticed any weight loss or fever?
